note: A COMPILATION THAT PRINTS ITS WITNESSES WHOLE. Kirkland's own argument is tier 3; the documents in Appendix F are older and are quoted as he prints them: Hubbard's letter of 1881 (reporting what Mrs. Kinzie and Mrs. Helm told him), Victoire Porthier's statement (an eyewitness from inside the fort, through Andreas), and the 1891 letters of Fernando Jones and J. C. Haines (who saw the fenced grave in 1835). Kirkland himself is no neutral: he reads the killing as 'not entirely disconnected' from the rivalry between Kinzie's trade and the government's factory.
what_it_supplies: Mrs. Kinzie's account through Hubbard: Lalime met Kinzie outside the garrison and shot him, 'the ball cutting the side of his neck'; Kinzie stabbed him, hid in the woods and was later acquitted by the officers
Victoire Porthier's eyewitness account: sunset at the fort gate, Lieutenant Helm calling a warning, the pistol, the two falling together, Kinzie taken to Milwaukee by her father that night
the grave: 'in plain view from his front door and piazza' (Hubbard), a picket fence, 'two hundred yards west of the Kinzie house', and the bones found at Cass and Illinois streets on 29 April 1891
Lalime's letters of 26 May and 7 July 1811, and Main Poc's reply
what_it_does_not_supply: any document of 1812 from the factor or the surgeon's mate (those are in the War Department letters, read here only through dailing_2018_chicago_reader_lalime)
